steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Type anatomy: baseline, x-height, ascenders, descenders, cap height — understanding these helps you choose and use type effectively.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Serif fonts have decorative strokes; sans-serif are cleaner and more modern; script fonts suggest elegance or informality.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Typographic hierarchy uses size, weight, colour and position to guide the reader through information in order of importance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Kerning (space between letters), tracking (overall letter spacing) and leading (line spacing) dramatically affect readability.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring typography and lettering. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with typography and lettering. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with typography and lettering. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to typography and lettering, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcome | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
